key_insight: The paper combines Bayesian optimization with discrete biorthogonal wavelet analysis to auto-lock laser frequency faster and more robustly than traditional scanning methods.
engineering_relevance: This approach improves practical laser stabilization for field-deployed quantum communication, computing, and precision-measurement systems.
method: Use Bayesian optimization to search the reference frequency from prior observations instead of blind parameter scanning.
Apply discrete biorthogonal wavelet transformation to detect transition signals and identify the correct reference via fixed frequency spacing and relative amplitudes.
Close the loop with a PZT-current double-servo system to maintain lock and narrow the linewidth.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 5× faster reference searching, >99.5% identification accuracy under strong disturbances, and a final linewidth of 20 kHz.
watch_item: Performance may depend on calibration quality and system-specific transition signatures, so robustness should be validated on other atomic setups and in long-term field operation.
paper_title: Rapid and robust laser-frequency auto-locking using Bayesian-optimization and discrete-wavelet-transformation algorithms
